value: Steam boiler raising process steam from fossil fuels (mostly natural gas) in a food and drink plant.

note: Boilers typically last for at least 30 years (printed); recorded as a minimum. Sect. 5 (p.98) says a 30-40 year lifespan is no exception (min 30, max 40 there).

value: CHP in food and drink plants: high-pressure steam boiler with steam turbine, gas turbine or gas engine with waste heat recovery for steam or hot water.

note: CHPs and turbines have a typical life span of around 20 years, with a major refurbishment after ten years (printed).

value: In-line pasteuriser: product rapidly heated to pasteurisation temperature, held, passed through a regeneration zone giving heat to incoming cold product and cooled; usually in a plate heat exchanger.

note: Printed as a heating temperature below 100 degC (pasteurisation); sterilisation uses over 100 degC. Upper bound only; no minimum printed.

value: Baking oven exposing food to hot air (or infrared radiation); direct heating, indirect heating, electric and infrared ovens exist.

note: Hot air at 110-240 degC (Sect. 3.2.5). Sect. 3.2.10 (p.36) gives 110-350 degC for baking ovens: inconsistent within the report.

value: Cleaning-in-place (CIP): cleaning solution pumped through closed process equipment, pipes and tanks without dismantling.

note: CIP systems typically work at 50-90 degC.
